questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the torque converter?
options: To provide the final gear reduction at the wheels
To hydraulically transfer torque from the engine flywheel to the transmission
questions.explanation: The torque converter connects the engine to the transmission and uses oil to transfer torque from the flywheel.

questions.prompt: Which torque converter component is the driving member?
questions.explanation: The impeller is splined to the flywheel, turns at engine RPM and drives the oil against the turbine.

questions.prompt: Which torque converter component is the driven member?
questions.explanation: The turbine receives oil flow from the impeller and turns the output shaft.

questions.prompt: What does the stator do?
options: Redirects oil from the turbine back to the impeller, multiplying torque
Locks the engine to the transmission
questions.explanation: The stator is the stationary reaction member; changing the oil direction increases torque capacity.

questions.prompt: The output shaft of a torque converter is splined to the...
questions.explanation: The output shaft is splined to the turbine and sends torque to the transmission input shaft.

questions.prompt: A torque converter is a fluid coupling with the addition of a...
questions.explanation: A fluid coupling has an impeller and turbine; adding a stator makes it a torque converter.

questions.prompt: Which is a benefit of the torque converter absorbing shock?
questions.explanation: Absorbing shock gives the powertrain a longer life.

questions.prompt: Which wheel-type machines are NOT normally fitted with torque converters?
options: Motor graders and hydraulic drive machines
questions.explanation: Wheel machines have torque converters except motor graders and hydraulic drive machines.

questions.prompt: In a one-way clutch torque converter, what does the one-way clutch do?
options: Locks the stator in one direction and lets it freewheel in the other
Connects the engine directly to the transmission
questions.explanation: The clutch locks the stator in one direction of rotation and allows it to freewheel in the opposite direction.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a variable capacity torque converter?
options: To let the operator limit torque increase, reducing wheel spin and diverting power to hydraulics
To lock the converter in direct drive
questions.explanation: Limiting torque increase reduces wheel spin and sends more power to the implement hydraulics.

questions.prompt: What does a lockup clutch torque converter provide when the lockup clutch is engaged?
options: A direct connection between engine and transmission, the highest drivetrain efficiency
questions.explanation: With the lockup clutch engaged the converter is in direct drive, giving the highest drivetrain efficiency.

questions.prompt: When does torque converter stall occur?
options: When the output shaft speed is zero
When oil temperature is too high
questions.explanation: Stall occurs when the output shaft speed is zero; the stall test is used when a converter problem is suspected.

questions.prompt: What does the torque converter ratio (inlet relief) valve control?
questions.explanation: The ratio valve controls the maximum pressure to the converter; the outlet relief valve maintains pressure in it.

questions.prompt: What differentiates a torque divider from a torque converter?
options: It has an integrated planetary gear set in front of the converter
It uses air instead of oil
questions.explanation: A torque divider is a conventional torque converter with a planetary gear set in front of it.

questions.prompt: A benefit of the torque divider permitting direct drive is...
options: Increased efficiency and better fuel economy
questions.explanation: Direct drive operation increases efficiency and fuel economy.

questions.prompt: In a planetary gear set, what is needed to transmit power?
options: One member held, one driving and one driven
questions.explanation: To transmit power through a planetary set one member is held, one drives and one is driven.

questions.prompt: What happens if no member of a planetary gear set is restrained?
options: The gears idle and no power is transmitted
questions.explanation: With nothing held the gears idle and no power is transmitted.

questions.prompt: What is the result if two members of a planetary gear set are locked together?
questions.explanation: Locking two members gives direct drive.

questions.prompt: If the planet carrier is held and the sun gear drives, the ring gear turns...
questions.explanation: Holding the carrier with the sun gear driving drives the ring gear in reverse.

questions.prompt: In a planetary powershift transmission, what does the modulating relief valve with the load piston do?
options: Gives a gradual pressure rise in the clutches and limits maximum speed clutch pressure (P1)
questions.explanation: The modulating relief valve and load piston provide a controlled pressure rise and limit P1.

questions.prompt: Which valve controls directional clutch pressure (P2)?
questions.explanation: The pressure differential valve controls directional clutch pressure (P2).

questions.prompt: Why is the clutch engagement chart important when troubleshooting a transmission?
options: It shows which clutches are engaged for each speed and direction, so the failed clutch pack can be found
questions.explanation: Knowing which clutches engage for each gear lets you diagnose which clutch pack has failed.

questions.prompt: How do countershaft transmissions differ from planetary transmissions?
options: They use constant mesh spur gears
questions.explanation: Countershaft transmissions use constant mesh spur gears on clutch shafts.

questions.prompt: In a countershaft powershift transmission, how many clutches must be engaged to transmit power?
options: One directional clutch and one speed clutch
questions.explanation: To transmit power one directional clutch and one speed clutch must be engaged.

questions.prompt: Countershaft transmission clutches are engaged ___ and disengaged ___.
questions.explanation: The clutches are engaged hydraulically and disengaged by spring force.

questions.prompt: What is an Individual Clutch Modulation (ICM) transmission?
options: A planetary powershift transmission with each clutch modulated individually
questions.explanation: The ICM transmission is a planetary powershift transmission; its advantages include smoother shifts and longer component life.

questions.prompt: Which benefit is linked to Individual Clutch Modulation?
options: It removes the need for a torque converter
It reduces torque spikes and abrupt shifts, reducing drivetrain wear
questions.explanation: ICM depresses torque spikes and abrupt shifts and gives smoother shifts.

questions.prompt: What is a transfer gear case (drop box) used for?
options: Connecting power units, changing the direction and speed of power flow, or dropping the axis of flow
questions.explanation: Transfer gears connect units, change direction and speed of power flow, or drop the axis of flow.

questions.prompt: When is an input transfer gear system most commonly used?
options: When the axles are in line with the transmission
When the transmission is not in line with the engine and torque converter
questions.explanation: For example, the 988F transmission is mounted lower than the engine, so an input transfer gear is used.

questions.prompt: Which is a benefit of transfer gears being able to drive auxiliary pumps?
options: It removes the need for additional pump drives
It removes the need for filters
questions.explanation: Driving auxiliary pumps from the transfer gears eliminates the need for extra pump drives.
